result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.add_directed_configuration_model()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Add a random directed multigraph with given in-degree and out-degree sequences. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.add_directed_configuration_model()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Add a random directed multigraph with given in-degree and out-degree sequences. title: >- [Graph.add_directed_configuration_model()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- Add a random directed multigraph with given in-degree and out-degree sequences. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Add a random directed multigraph with given in-degree and out-degree sequences. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L11257-L11362){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.add_directed_configuration_model( in_degree_sequence, out_degree_sequence, seed=None, type=None, label=True, rel=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Directed configuration model](../assets/graphs/add-directed-configuration-model.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Three directed configuration models, each node's in-degree and out-degree in a pill written in/out. Four nodes at 1/1 form a directed four-cycle; 0/2, 1/1, 1/1, and 2/0 send every arc from the source toward the sink; on five nodes two pairs of opposite arcs appear, drawn bowed apart. Out-stubs are paired with in-stubs at random, so every node meets its pill exactly; self-loops and repeated arcs are possible, though this draw has none." width="100%"} Node `i` gets `in_degree_sequence[i]` incoming stubs and `out_degree_sequence[i]` outgoing stubs. Both lists of stubs are shuffled and paired, each outgoing stub with an incoming one, and each pair becomes an edge from the outgoing stub's node to the incoming stub's. Every node's in-degree and out-degree come out exactly as given, but self-loops and parallel edges can appear; they are rare when the degrees are small compared with the number of edges, and `count_all_loops()` and `count_multi_edges()` report them. If the two sequences differ in length, the shorter one is padded with zeros. The process follows NetworkX's `directed_configuration_model()`; see `configuration_model()` for the undirected version. In an undirected graph the same edges are added without their direction, so each node's degree is its in-degree plus its out-degree. The graph is appended without touching or connecting to existing nodes, and the whole construction is recorded as a single step. Directed configuration models are useful for: - null models that keep each node's in- and out-degree, e.g. for testing whether reciprocity or motif counts are more than the degrees explain - random directed graphs with heavy-tailed in-degrees, such as citation or follower networks - generating directed test graphs with exactly prescribed degrees ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [in_degree_sequence]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : In-degree of each new node, as a list of non-negative integers. [out_degree_sequence]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Out-degree of each new node, as a list of non-negative integers. Must have the same sum as `in_degree_sequence=`. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Integer seed for the random number generator. The same `seed=` with the same other arguments always gives the same graph. If `None` (default), the graph differs on every call. [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `type` attribute of every new node. If `None` (default), no `type` attribute is set. [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), each new node is labelled with its node ID as a string; a label that is already used raises `ValueError` before anything is added. If `False`, the nodes are left unlabelled. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `rel` attribute of every new edge. If `None` (default), no `rel` attribute is set. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. The graph is modified in place. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If either sequence contains a negative entry, or the two sums differ. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Every node gets exactly the in-degree and out-degree it was given: ::: {#e66f1b2d .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec in_degrees = [0, 1, 1, 2, 3] out_degrees = [2, 2, 1, 1, 1] graph = ec.Graph(directed=True).add_directed_configuration_model( in_degrees, out_degrees, seed=9 ) nodes = sorted(graph.get_node_ids()) [graph.get_in_degree(v) for v in nodes], [graph.get_out_degree(v) for v in nodes] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ([0, 1, 1, 2, 3], [2, 2, 1, 1, 1]) ``` ::: ::: The random pairing can make self-loops and parallel edges: ::: {#3108f512 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.count_all_loops(), graph.count_multi_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` (1, 0) ``` ::: :::
